source: Homebrew rules — optional campaign rules that override the standard Earthdawn 4E rulebooks. Authoring guide: docs/HOMEBREW-RULES.md. Each rule is pure data (inputs + plain-English notes); nothing here stores a derived value. A rule applies globally (every character) when `enabled` is true. A rule may `formula` (replace a rating with a term sum), `effects` (adjust values via the standard taxonomy, docs/EFFECT-TAXONOMY.md), `set` (v2: override a registry target — karma.step / karma.maxCap / karma.ritualCost / legend.additionalTierShift — with a scalar or a race-keyed map), and/or `knackParents` (v3: a boolean that lets a character's owned skills govern knacks — docs/HOMEBREW-RULES.md §5.6). Refs resolve against the character (engine/characteristics.js); the set-target registry lives in store.js (HOMEBREW_SET_TARGETS).
note: This file is loaded optionally (knacks/thread-items precedent): if it is absent the app behaves exactly as before. Rules ship `enabled: false` until the owner turns them on.

rules.name: Durability-scaled Health Ratings
rules.overrides: Players' Guide p.64 — Health Ratings (Unconsciousness & Death)
rules.summary: These rules are added to better reflect a true unconsciousness & death rating based on a characters base Toughness and how much they train their Durability

unconsciousness.note: Term1 + Term2 = (Durability Rank × Toughness Step) + table uncon

terms.note: Term2: The standard Unconsciousness base from the characteristics table.

death.note: Term1 + Term2 + Term3 (Durability Rank × Toughness Step) + Toughness Step + table death

terms.note: Term3: The standard Death base from the characteristics table.

rules.name: Race-driven Karma economy (ED-classic buy-back)
rules.overrides: Players' Guide p.83 — Karma Ritual (house rule)
rules.summary: The Karma Ritual is no longer a free refill: you buy Karma back with Legend at a race-driven cost, up to a race-driven maximum, and the Karma die is race-driven. This rule makes karma use rarer and increases its etherial position
rules.note: Uses the ed-homebrew/2 `set` lever (docs/HOMEBREW-RULES.md §5.5, plans/PLAN-HOMEBREW-KARMA.md). karma.maxCap is the racial ceiling (engine applies min(Modifier×Circle, cap)); karma.step is the Karma die Step (= the racial Modifier); karma.ritualCost is the Legend spent per Karma point on the paid ritual (a dated, undoable Legend sink). Ships disabled.

rules.name: Additional-Discipline talents priced one tier higher
rules.overrides: Players' Guide — New Discipline Talent Cost Table & Equivalent Talent Circle Table (house rule)
rules.summary: A talent learned in an additional Discipline (2nd and later) costs Legend as if it were one tier higher than its own tier — Novice→Journeyman, Journeyman→Warden, Warden→Master, Master stays Master — replacing the New-Discipline Rank-1 and Equivalent-Tier tables entirely.
rules.note: Uses the ed-homebrew/2 `set` lever (docs/HOMEBREW-RULES.md §5.5, plans/PLAN-HOMEBREW-LEGEND-TIER.md). `legend.additionalTierShift: 1` prices every rank of an additional-Discipline talent at its own tier bumped one step (e.g. a Novice talent at Rank 3 costs 200+300+500=1000 instead of the surcharge-table price). Value 0/absent keeps the standard tables. Owner-enabled for the current campaign.

rules.name: Learning a spell costs no Legend
rules.overrides: Players' Guide p.252 — Spell Legend Point Cost (house rule)
rules.summary: A magician spends no Legend Points to learn a spell; the spell's Circle-based Legend cost is waived. The silver copy cost is unchanged.
rules.note: Uses the ed-homebrew/2 `set` lever (docs/HOMEBREW-RULES.md §5.5, plans/PLAN-HOMEBREW-SPELL-LEARN-COST.md). `legend.spellLearnCostMultiplier: 0` multiplies every learned spell's Legend cost by 0 in the Legend-spent audit's spells sink (PLAN-LEARN-SPELLS §5.1) and in the Learn modal's shown price. `spells.learnSilverMultiplier: 1` scales the Learn modal's suggested silver price — 1 leaves it unchanged; the knob exists to tune silver later without a new rule. Each multiplier defaults to 1 when absent. Owner-enabled for the current campaign.

rules.name: Skills may govern knacks
rules.summary: A character's owned skills can govern knacks: a knack is available through a skill whenever that knack lists the skill's name as one of its parents and the skill's rank meets the knack's required rank. This mirrors the standard talent gate but keys off the character's skills. Present and true = active (no `enabled` field needed); absent = the talent-only default.
rules.note: Uses the ed-homebrew/3 `knackParents` lever (docs/HOMEBREW-RULES.md §5.6): a boolean flag, not a skill list. When true, ANY knack whose parents include a skill the character owns becomes learnable through it (rank >= requiredRank, under the per-parent cap). This rule is active by its existence — it intentionally has no `enabled` field.
